why: Organic search brings visitors you do not pay for each click, often the largest traffic source of a website. Almost every marketing job asks for SEO basics, and SEO specialists are hired on their own.
outcome: explain crawling, indexing and ranking, choose keywords by intent, write titles and descriptions, read robots.txt and canonical tags, check Core Web Vitals, plan links and measure results in Google Search Console.

lessons.title: How search engines work
text: A search engine does three things. It crawls: robots (Googlebot) follow links and download pages. It indexes: it reads each page, understands its topic and stores it. It ranks: for each query, it orders the indexed pages by how useful they are likely to be.
A page can fail at each step: not found (no links to it), not indexed (blocked, duplicate, low quality) or indexed but ranked too low to be seen. SEO work starts by finding which step fails.
points: No crawl, no index; no index, no ranking.
Google ranks pages, not websites: each page targets its own queries.
Ranking signals include relevance, quality, links, page experience and freshness when it matters.
Google’s guidance: write helpful content for people first (E-E-A-T: experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trust).

lessons.title: Keyword research and search intent
text: Keyword research finds the words your audience types, how often (volume), how hard it is to rank (difficulty) and what they want (intent). Tools: Google Search Console, Google Keyword Planner, Semrush, Ahrefs, or simply Google’s suggestions and 'People also ask'.

Intent matters more than volume. Informational queries want an answer, commercial ones compare options, transactional ones want to buy, navigational ones look for a brand. Look at the current first page: it shows which kind of page Google thinks answers the query.
points: Long-tail keywords (longer, precise) have less volume but convert better and are easier.
Group keywords by topic: one page per intent, not one page per keyword.
Two pages targeting the same query compete with each other (cannibalization).
Check the first results before writing: a guide will not rank where Google shows product pages.

example.code:
Keyword                              Volume/month  Difficulty  Intent
running shoes                        90,000        very high   mixed
best running shoes for flat feet     2,400         medium      commercial
running shoes flat feet women        880           low         commercial
how to know if you have flat feet    1,900         low         informational
stridelab arch 3 review              140           low         transactional
example.note: The broad term is out of reach for a small site; the precise commercial queries are the realistic targets.

lessons.title: On-page SEO: titles, descriptions and content
text: The title tag is the clickable line in search results and a strong relevance signal: put the main keyword near the start, keep it around 50–60 characters, and make it attractive. The meta description does not change ranking but often becomes the snippet: around 150–160 characters that make people click.

On the page: one H1 that says what the page is about, subheadings (H2, H3) that structure it, the answer early, descriptive alt text on images, short readable URLs, and internal links to related pages with descriptive anchor text.
points: Write the title for the person searching, not only for the robot.
Each page needs a unique title and description.
Cover the topic fully: the questions the reader will ask next.
Update pages that lose traffic rather than writing new ones on the same topic.

example.code:
<head>
  <title>Running Shoes for Flat Feet: 2026 Guide | StrideLab</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Compare 12 running shoes tested on flat feet: support, cushioning and price. Free size guide and 30-day returns.">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://stridelab.example/guides/running-shoes-flat-feet">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
</head>
example.note: Title with the keyword first and the brand last; a description that promises a concrete benefit.

lessons.title: Technical SEO: crawling and indexing
text: robots.txt tells robots which paths not to crawl; it does not remove a page from the index. To keep a page out of results, use a noindex meta tag (and let robots crawl it so they can see the tag). An XML sitemap lists the pages you want indexed and helps robots find them.

The canonical tag tells search engines which URL is the main version when several URLs show the same content (filters, tracking parameters, http and https). Redirect moved pages with a 301 (permanent) redirect, and fix broken links that return 404.
points: Blocking a page in robots.txt and adding noindex at the same time does not work: the robot never sees the noindex.
Use HTTPS everywhere and one version of the domain (with or without www).
Mobile-first indexing: Google mainly uses the mobile version of the page.
Search Console → Pages shows which pages are indexed and why others are not.

example.code:
# https://stridelab.example/robots.txt
User-agent: *
Disallow: /cart/
Disallow: /search?

Sitemap: https://stridelab.example/sitemap.xml
example.note: The cart and the internal search results are not worth crawling; the sitemap address helps robots find everything else.

lessons.title: Page experience and Core Web Vitals
text: Core Web Vitals measure how a page feels to real users: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP, loading: the main content appears within 2.5 s), Interaction to Next Paint (INP, responsiveness: under 200 ms; it replaced First Input Delay in March 2024) and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS, visual stability: under 0.1).

Measure them with PageSpeed Insights and the Core Web Vitals report in Search Console, which use field data from Chrome users. Common fixes: compress and size images, load less JavaScript, reserve space for images and ads, use a CDN and caching.
points: Field data (real users) is what counts; lab tests help find the cause.
A threshold is 'good' when 75 % of visits meet it.
Speed also improves conversion, not only SEO.
Fast pages do not beat relevant ones: experience is a tie-breaker, content comes first.

lessons.title: Links, local SEO and structured data
text: Links from other websites act as votes of confidence: a few links from relevant, trusted sites are worth more than many from weak ones. Earn them with content people want to cite: studies, tools, guides, data. Buying links breaks Google’s spam policies and can get a site demoted.

For a local business, the Google Business Profile (address, opening hours, photos, reviews) drives the map results. Structured data (schema.org in JSON-LD) describes products, reviews, events or FAQs so search engines can show rich results such as stars and prices.
points: Internal links spread authority inside your own site: link your important pages often.
Ask satisfied customers for reviews and answer them, positive or negative.
Keep name, address and phone identical everywhere (NAP consistency).
Test structured data with Google’s Rich Results Test.

example.note: Product structured data: name, rating and offer. Only mark up what is visible on the page.

lessons.title: Measuring SEO and reporting
text: Google Search Console is the free source of truth for Google Search: impressions, clicks, average position and click-through rate by query and by page, indexing problems and Core Web Vitals. Web analytics (such as GA4) shows what organic visitors do next: sign-ups, purchases.
SEO is slow: changes take weeks to show. Report trends over months, compare like with like (same period last year for seasonal businesses) and link SEO to business results, not only rankings.
points: High impressions with low CTR: rewrite the title and description.
Position 5–15 queries are the quickest wins: improve those pages.
Annotate releases and Google updates to explain changes.
An SEO audit lists problems by impact and effort, not as one long list.

items: Robots follow links and download pages
The page is read, understood and stored
Indexed pages are ordered for each query
Clickable title in results, ~50–60 characters, keyword first
Snippet text, ~150–160 characters, no ranking effect
One main heading that says what the page is about
Describes an image for screen readers and search engines
Link to another page of your site with a descriptive anchor
Paths robots should not crawl (not de-indexing)
Meta tag that keeps a page out of results
Permanent move, passes signals to the new URL
List of the pages you want indexed
The page reacts fast to clicks and taps
Queries, clicks, positions, indexing, Core Web Vitals
Speed and Core Web Vitals of one page

pitfalls: Chasing a broad keyword a small site cannot rank for, instead of precise long-tail queries.
Using robots.txt to hide a page from results (use noindex).
Several pages targeting the same query and competing with each other.
Buying links or stuffing keywords: both break Google’s spam policies.
Reporting rankings only, without clicks, conversions and revenue.

exercises.q: Which search has commercial intent (the person compares options before buying)?
options: how to know if you have flat feet
best running shoes for flat feet
exercises.answer: “Best … for …” compares products before a purchase: commercial intent. The two “how / what” searches are informational, “stridelab login” is navigational.

exercises.q: Tap the line that will keep this page out of Google’s results.
exercises.snippet:
<head>
  <title>Home</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Compare 12 running shoes tested on flat feet.">
  <meta name="robots" content="noindex">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://stridelab.example/guides/running-shoes-flat-feet">
</head>
exercises.answer: noindex asks search engines not to show the page. It is often left over from a test site. Remove it (or use index, follow). The title “Home” is weak too: it should describe the page.

exercises.q: Match each Core Web Vital with what it measures.
pairs: How fast the main content appears
How fast the page reacts to a click or tap
Whether elements jump while the page loads
exercises.answer: Largest Contentful Paint (good: ≤ 2.5 s), Interaction to Next Paint (≤ 200 ms) and Cumulative Layout Shift (≤ 0.1).

exercises.q: Put the steps in the order a page goes through before it can bring visitors from Google.
steps: Googlebot finds a link to the page
The page ranks for a query
exercises.answer: Discovery, crawl, index, rank, click. When a page brings no traffic, find which step fails first (Search Console → URL inspection).

exercises.q: A product page exists at two URLs (with and without ?color=blue). Which tag tells Google the main URL?
exercises.answer: The canonical tag, <link rel="canonical" href="…">, on both versions, pointing to the main URL.

exercises.q: A blog page has 40,000 impressions a month in Search Console, an average position of 4 and a CTR of 0.8 %. What do you do?

steps.text: What is the first thing you look at?

choices.label: The title and description shown in results
choices.feedback: At position 4 a CTR under 1 % is low: the snippet does not make people click.

choices.label: Buy links to reach position 1
choices.feedback: Buying links breaks Google’s spam policies, and the problem here is the click, not the position.

choices.label: Delete the page
choices.feedback: The page already ranks well; deleting it loses the impressions.

steps.text: The title is “Blog post 12”. What do you change?

choices.label: A title with the query and a clear benefit, plus a description that answers the intent
choices.feedback: Then compare the CTR over the next 4 weeks in Search Console.

choices.label: Repeat the keyword five times in the title
choices.feedback: Keyword stuffing reads badly and does not earn clicks.

exercises.answer: Low CTR at a good position means the snippet is the problem: rewrite the title and description for the query’s intent, then measure the CTR change in Search Console.

exercises.q: You start SEO for a local bakery in Tunis. List five actions, in the order you would do them.
exercises.answer: 1) Create and complete the Google Business Profile (address, hours, photos, category). 2) Make sure the site is indexed, fast and mobile-friendly (Search Console, PageSpeed Insights). 3) Give each product family and the shop page a clear title and description with the city (“Pâtisserie à Tunis …”). 4) Ask happy customers for reviews and answer them. 5) Get mentioned by local sites (press, guides, partners) and keep name, address and phone identical everywhere.

interview.q: What is the difference between crawling, indexing and ranking?
interview.a: Crawling is robots downloading pages by following links; indexing is the search engine reading and storing the page; ranking is ordering indexed pages for a query. A page with no traffic is diagnosed by finding which of those steps fails.

interview.q: robots.txt or noindex: which one removes a page from Google?
interview.a: noindex. robots.txt only blocks crawling; a blocked URL can still be indexed from links, and the robot cannot see a noindex tag on a page it is not allowed to crawl.

interview.q: What are the Core Web Vitals?
interview.a: LCP for loading (good under 2.5 s), INP for responsiveness (under 200 ms, it replaced FID in 2024) and CLS for visual stability (under 0.1), measured on real Chrome users at the 75th percentile.

interview.q: How do you choose which keywords to target?
interview.a: By intent first, then by realistic difficulty and value: I look at what the first page shows for the query, pick precise long-tail queries where we can rank and that lead to conversions, and assign one page per intent to avoid cannibalization.

interview.q: Organic traffic dropped 30 % last week. What do you check?
interview.a: Whether it is real (tracking change, seasonality, same week last year), then Search Console: which pages and queries lost clicks, indexing errors, manual actions, a recent site release (noindex, redirects, robots.txt) and whether a Google update was announced.

interview.q: How do you get good backlinks?
interview.a: By creating things people want to cite (data studies, tools, guides), digital PR, partnerships and fixing mentions that have no link. Never by buying links, which breaks Google’s spam policies.
